title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 213
paragraphs: While the king was at a loss as to what to do next, Epialtes son of Eurydemos, a Malian, came to speak with him, supposing he would win a great reward. This man told him of the path leading over the mountain to Thermopylae, and so brought about the destruction of the Greeks remaining there. Afterwards, fearing the Lacedaemonians, he fled to Thessaly; and while he was in exile, the Deputies placed a price on his life when the Amphictyons met for their assembly at Pylai. Some time later, having returned to Antikyra, he was slain by Athenades, a man of Trachis. Now this Athenades killed Epialtes for another reason, which I shall describe later in this history; but for this deed he was honored by the Lacedaemonians nonetheless.
